newsitem.title: USA: New U.S. company to develop abortion drug.
newsitem.headline: New U.S. company to develop abortion drug.

text.p: A non-profit group holding U.S. patent rights to the French abortion pill RU 486 said on Wednesday it has formed a new company to market the controversial drug and hopes to bring it to the United States later this year.

Formation of the new company, Advances for Choice, marks the settlement of a lawsuit between the non-profit group, the Population Council, and Joseph Pike, a businessman who held sub-licenses to develop the pill, the group said.
The New York-based Population Council sued Pike for fraud last year after he was accused in a separate lawsuit of using the venture as an illegal money-making scheme.

The new company will design the U.S. distribution of the drug mifepristone, which causes abortion by inducing uterine contractions and would give women an alternative to surgical abortion in early pregnancy.

Due to controversy over the drug, which is available in much of Europe, many details about the drug's development in the United States have been kept secret. The identities of the limited partners in the new company, for example, have not been disclosed publicly.
The Population Council hopes to have the drug win U.S. government approval and be on the market by the end of 1997, said its president, Margaret Catley-Carlson.

The drug is made by Roussell Uclaf Co. of France which, under pressure from the anti-abortion rights movement, did not bring the drug to the U.S. market. Instead, in an unconventional move, Roussell, a unit of Hoechst AG, gave the U.S. patent rights to the Population Council.
The council has run clinical tests and expects to release those results in a matter of weeks, it said.
The partners in Advances for Choice include those from an earlier company, Advances in Health Technology, of which the businessman Pike was a major investor.

Under terms of the settlement, Pike sold a substantial portion of his equity to the remaining investors and will play no management role in the new company or the project, the group said. He will retain an unspecified "modest" equity interest, it said.
The settlement with Pike came after months of negotiations with the Population Council.

The chief executive of the new company, Jack Van Hulst, would not reveal the cost of developing the drug and seeking approval from the federal Food and Drug Administration. The company is on "solid financial footing," he said.
